article_title: Parent Praise to 1- to 3-Year-Olds Predicts Children's Motivational Frameworks 5 Years Later
citation: Gunderson Elizabeth A., Gripshover Sarah J., Romero Carissa, Dweck Carol S., Goldin-Meadow Susan, Levine Susan C. (2013). Parent Praise to 1-3 Year-Olds Predicts Children's Motivational Frameworks 5 Years Later. Child development. https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.12064
title: 24-item motivational frameworks questionnaire (intelligence and sociomoral domains)
description: A composite instrument administered at ages 7-8 across two visits about three months apart, combining 18 intelligence-domain items adapted from prior work and 6 sociomoral yes-or-no items. It assesses "beliefs about trait stability, their preferences for learning versus performance goals, their attributions for success and failure, and their ability to generate strategies for improvement". Items were z-scored and averaged so higher scores indicate more incremental frameworks; the 24-item composite had α = .70.
requirements: Administered orally to children in 2nd or 3rd grade; open-ended items scored with coder reliability (α's ≥ .75)
constraints: Composite reliability α = .70; intelligence-domain reliability α = .61; sixteen children did not complete all 24 items
target_learners: children aged 7-8 years in 2nd or 3rd grade
target_learning_goals: implicit theories of intelligence and sociomoral goodness
goal orientation, attributions, and strategy generation
examples: Item 9 asked, "How much would you like to do mazes that are very hard so you can learn more about doing mazes?"
key_sources: Gunderson Elizabeth A., Gripshover Sarah J., Romero Carissa, Dweck Carol S., Goldin-Meadow Susan, Levine Susan C. (2013). Parent Praise to 1-3 Year-Olds Predicts Children's Motivational Frameworks 5 Years Later. Child development. https://doi.org/10.1111/cdev.12064

article_title: Medical students’ satisfaction level with e-learning during the COVID-19 pandemic and its related factors: a systematic review.
citation: Tabatabaeichehr Mahbubeh, Babaei Samane, Dartomi Mahdieh, Alesheikh Peiman, Tabatabaee Amir, Mortazavi Hamed, Khoshgoftar Zohreh. (2022). Medical students’ satisfaction level with e-learning during the COVID-19 pandemic and its related factors: a systematic review. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2022.19.37
title: Corpus of 24 cross-sectional studies of medical students' e-learning satisfaction appraised with the AXIS tool
description: The review assembled a corpus of 24 cross-sectional studies enrolling 15,473 medical science students, mean age 20.84±2.06 years, 58.23% women, 73.45% studying clinical medicine, drawn from 14 countries. Quality was appraised with the AXIS tool, a 20-item instrument rating report quality, study design quality, and possible biases at three levels. The review reports that "21 studies ... were of high quality, 2 studies ... were of fair quality, and 1 study ... was of low quality."
requirements: Studies had to be cross-sectional designs focused on medical students' satisfaction with e-learning and related factors; letters, case reports, conference proceedings, experiments, qualitative designs, and reviews were excluded
constraints: Gray literature was not included; only English and Persian publications were searched
target_learners: medical science students, primarily undergraduate clinical medicine students
target_learning_goals: satisfaction with e-learning during the COVID-19 pandemic
examples: Searches of Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Iranmedex, and the Scientific Information Database yielded 3,554 studies, of which 24 remained after exclusions; satisfaction questionnaires were researcher-created in 23 studies and one used the reduced Students' Evaluation of Educational Quality.
key_sources: Tabatabaeichehr Mahbubeh, Babaei Samane, Dartomi Mahdieh, Alesheikh Peiman, Tabatabaee Amir, Mortazavi Hamed, Khoshgoftar Zohreh. (2022). Medical students’ satisfaction level with e-learning during the COVID-19 pandemic and its related factors: a systematic review. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://doi.org/10.3352/jeehp.2022.19.37
